question: Should experimental Claws become a core lifecycle owner for globally shared MCP declarations, provenance, reconciliation, and final removal?
rationale: The patch is not merely an implementation detail: it creates persistent core authority over executable and remote capability that already has an operator-managed MCP registry, while the governing RFC and prerequisite stack remain open.

options.title: Defer pending RFC
options.body: Keep the PR open but do not merge until the RFC and prerequisite establish the canonical ownership and coexistence contract.

options.title: Approve core ownership
options.body: Accept Claw ownership after URL redaction, live lifecycle proof, migration checks, and explicit operator-managed coexistence guarantees are complete.

options.title: Use plugin ownership
options.body: Move package-specific MCP lifecycle management to the plugin or bundle boundary and retain only generic config primitives in core.

recommendation.title: Defer pending RFC
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but do not merge until the RFC and prerequisite establish the canonical ownership and coexistence contract.
